tone.says: Three register tones: high (or rising), mid (level) and low (or falling); tone is phonemic (si 'carry' / 'dog' / 'sand') and tone sandhi occurs when morphemes are compounded.

sources.locator: p. 39 (section 'Syllable', below Fig. 1) and p. 42 (Conclusion, point i)
sources.note: Treats tone as an obligatory constituent of every Rongmei syllable (syllable = onset, nucleus, coda and tone τ); no tone inventory, values or sandhi given; refers the phonology to Deb 2010 MPhil. Also: roots mostly monosyllabic, no clusters, CVC commonest, sesquisyllables present.

sources.note: No prose statement (front matter absent from the PDF), but every headword is tone-coded syllable by syllable with a six-way set of labels /ht/, /mt/, /lt/, /rt/, /gt/, /lvt/ (disyllables e.g. /mt+ht/, /rt+ht/); counts over the file: lt 516, ht 467, mt 452, rt 418, gt 328, lvt 149 single-syllable codes; tonal minimal sets are visible, e.g. zung /ht/ 'toe/finger' vs zung e /mt/ 'devoted' vs zungc /rt/ 'mound' (p. 270), abah /gt/ vs abaw /lt/ vs abung /ht/ (p. 1). ht/mt/lt plainly = high/mid/low; rt presumably rising; the values of gt and lvt (glottal/checked? level?) are not established because…
